data.reasoning: The disagreement is caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen model's audit of .SRCINFO, not by genuine security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all three files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, .gitignore) and found them safe. The qwen model also found PKGBUILD and .gitignore safe before failing on .SRCINFO. The PKGBUILD is a standard VCS package: it clones from the declared upstream (codeberg.org), uses standard cargo build commands, and has SKIP checksums which are expected for -git packages. No injection patterns, suspicious network operations, or obfuscated code are present. The .SRCINFO is purely declarative metadata with no executable content.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is artificial - caused by an API failure (HTTP 400) in the qwen model when auditing .SRCINFO, not by differing security assessments. Both models agreed PKGBUILD and .gitignore are safe. The deepseek model completed all file reviews successfully.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .SRCINFO due to LLM API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) - this is a tool failure, not a coverage gap
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should not force an 'inconclusive' verdict when other models have successfully reviewed the same files and found no issues
The audit system should distinguish between 'model could not complete review' and 'model found potential issues' - the former should not block a safe verdict if coverage is otherwise complete
For .SRCINFO files specifically, models should recognize these are declarative metadata with no executable content and require minimal analysis
